intro: An internal memo about a new document system, written the way administrative German is written: almost no werden-passives, but one passive substitute after another. Twelve gaps, and each one asks you to build the substitute, not to spot it: sein + zu + infinitive for the instructions (the gap holds zu + infinitive — ist … zu finden, sind … zu melden, sind … zu übertragen, sind … zu speichern, sind … zu vermeiden), sich lassen for what is possible (the gap holds the conjugated lassen — singular or plural), -bar adjectives for the same idea in adjective form (änderbar, erreichbar), and bekommen + Partizip II where the staff are the recipients (bekommen … zugeschickt, erhalten … erklärt). The hints give you the verb or the English meaning; the form is yours. Read the memo as a genre first — greeting, purpose, rules, travel rules, contact, sign-off — then fill the gaps. Afterwards rewrite two sentences in your head with the plain passive (muss gemeldet werden) to feel why the memo does not: the substitutes are shorter and sound like a rule rather than an order.
tips[0].title: Instructions → sein + zu; possibilities → sich lassen / -bar
tips[0].text: A rule in a memo is sein + zu + infinitive: Probleme sind zu melden. With a separable verb the zu goes inside (einzureichen). What is possible is sich lassen (lässt sich / lassen sich — agree with the subject) or a -bar adjective (änderbar = kann geändert werden).
tips[0].trap: sein + zu can mean must or can — in a memo of rules it almost always means must. Only sich lassen and -bar are unambiguously "can".
tips[0].check.why: A rule is sein + zu + infinitive, and with a separable verb the zu goes inside: einzureichen.
tips[0].visual.rows[0].b: Das Passwort lässt sich jederzeit ändern.
tips[1].title: Recipients → bekommen / erhalten + Partizip II
tips[1].text: When the people addressed receive something, they become the subject: Sie bekommen die Unterlagen zugeschickt (= Ihnen werden die Unterlagen zugeschickt). The finite verb is bekommen or erhalten; the participle goes to the end.
tips[1].check.why: When the people addressed receive something, they become the subject of bekommen, and the participle goes to the end.
tips[2].title: The memo's skeleton
tips[2].text: Liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen, → purpose (wie angekündigt …) → rules in sein + zu → special cases (Für … gilt Folgendes:) → contact (… ist erreichbar) → thanks → Mit freundlichen Grüßen. Same frame every time; only the content changes.
tips[2].check.why: The contact line of a memo uses the -bar adjective: ist … erreichbar (can be reached).
remember[0]: Rule = sein + zu (zu + infinitive in the gap); possible = lässt sich / lassen sich, -bar; recipient = bekommen / erhalten + Partizip II.
remember[1]: Memos avoid werden: substitutes sound like rules, not orders.
hook: Read and write office memos the way German offices do (ist zu melden, lässt sich ändern): rules without a single werden.
